Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct, but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct, but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
es a stronger attraction between ions and thus a more stable ionic compound.
Reason (R): Lattice enthalpy is a direct measure of the electrostatic forces of repulsion among the constituent ions in an ionic solid. This statement is incorrect. questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements among the following
a) $\mathrm{C}_{60}$ molecule has 12 six-membered rings and 20 five-membered rings
b) $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 / \mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$buffer system helps to maintain $\mathrm{pH}$ of blood between 7.26 and 7.42
c) Graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperatures
questions.solution:
- a) \(C_{60}\) molecule has 12 six-membered rings and 20 five-membered rings. This is incorrect. The \(C_{60}\) fullerene molecule, also known as buckminsterfullerene, has a spherical structure with 12 five-membered rings and 20 six-membered rings.
- b) \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 / \mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}\) buffer system helps to maintain pH of blood between 7.26 and 7.42. This is correct. The carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system is a crucial component of blood plasma that resists changes in pH, keeping it within a narrow range required for proper physiological function.
- c) Graphite is used as a dry lubricant in machines running at high temperatures. This is correct. Graphite consists of layers that can slide over one another easily, giving it lubricating properties. It is particularly effective at high temperatures where conventional liquid lubricants would vaporize.
Statements \(\mathrm{b}\) and \(\mathrm{c}\) are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The decay of a radioactive material is shown in the graph. From the graph, the decay constant of the material is nearly
questions.solution:
- From the decay graph:
At \(t=0\), material \(\approx 100 \mathrm{~kg}\).
At \(t \approx 20\) hours, material \(\approx 50 \mathrm{~kg}\).
- So, the half-life of the substance is:
\(T_{1 / 2} \approx 20 \text { hours }\)
- Relation between decay constant (\(\lambda\)) and half-life:
\(\lambda=\frac{\ln 2}{T_{1 / 2}}\)
- Substituting:
\(\lambda=\frac{0.693}{20} \approx 0.03465 \mathrm{~h}^{-1}\)
- Converting hours to seconds:
\(1 \mathrm{~h}=3600 \mathrm{~s}\)
\(\lambda \approx \frac{0.03465}{3600} \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \approx 9.6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}\)
But since the given options are in \(\mathrm{ms}^{-1}\) (likely meant as \(\times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~h}^{-1}\)), the nearest match is:
\(\lambda \approx 3.2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\)
Correct option: (1)
